newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Espirito Santo state sees lower coffee crop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Espirito Santo state sees lower coffee crop.

text.p: Brazil's Espirito Santo state will produce 3.59 million 60-kg bags coffee in 1997/98, down 27.69 percent from 4.97 million in 1996/97, according to the first estimate from the state agricultural secretariat.
Output of arabica coffee is expected to see the largest percentage drop of 37.17 percent to 1.06 million bags from this year's 1.69 million.
Conillon coffee production is forecast to drop 22.81 percent to 2.53 million from a 1996/97 crop of 3.29 million bags.
"The fall in arabica production is mainly due to the fact that the crop is in an off-year," said Marcos Moulin, agronomist at the department responsible for crop estimates.
In Brazil, arabica coffee production has a two-year cycle in which there is a larger crop every other year.
However this is not the case for conillon coffee which normally only sees a small variation from year to year, he said.
"With conillon, the problem is the delay in the arrival of the rains which normally should come in the middle of September but which only started in October," he said.
"Originally we had expected to see a fall of around 15 percent but when the figures came back, it was a lot worse than that," Moulin said.
The next estimate from the secretariat should be published in March after a further survey is carried out in February.
So far there are few concrete estimates of the 1997/98 Brazilian crop but producers have been saying for some months that they expect the coming harvest to be smaller than that of 1996/97.
-- Caroline Bullloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
